content: The American Thoracic Society (ATS), founded in 1905, is an independently incorporated, international, educational, and scientific society. It serves a global membership of 18,000 individuals who are dedicated to the fields of respiratory and critical care medicine. The society's mission is to prevent and combat respiratory diseases by advancing research, education, patient care, and advocacy, with the ultimate goal of reducing morbidity and mortality associated with respiratory conditions. History In 1905, the American Sanatorium Association was established as a division of the American Lung Association. At that time, its focus was on the prevention, control, and treatment of tuberculosis. In 1938, the organization was renamed the American Trudeau Society in honor of Dr. Edward Livingston Trudeau. In 1960, the name was changed again to the American Thoracic Society. In 2000, the American Thoracic Society became independent from the American Lung Association. Mission Statement The American Thoracic Society (ATS) is a non-profit, international, professional, and scientific organization focused on respiratory, critical care, and sleep medicine. The ATS is committed to preventing and treating respiratory diseases through research, education, patient care, and advocacy. Its long-term goal is to reduce morbidity and mortality from respiratory, critical care, and sleep disorders, as well as life-threatening acute illnesses, across all age groups. To achieve these objectives, the ATS collaborates with national and international organizations that share similar goals. Research The ATS promotes the highest quality research to facilitate the discovery of new knowledge. It collaborates with other organizations to advocate for research. The society coordinates, develops, and manages research and research training grant programs in partnership with other organizations. It provides guidance and direction to agencies and organizations that fund research related to respiratory and critical care medicine. The ATS works to increase funding for research and training as a non-profit, tax-exempt organization. Education The ATS disseminates new scientific information through scientific meetings and the publication of peer-reviewed journals. It translates new scientific findings into patient education materials. The society develops innovative approaches to educate professionals and other healthcare providers about respiratory and critical care medicine. It encourages and provides the highest standards of training in respiratory and critical care medicine for professionals and healthcare providers. The ATS promotes the highest standards for research and clinical practice worldwide. It facilitates the interpretation and transfer of both new research findings and existing knowledge to practitioners. The society provides information and expertise on respiratory and critical care diseases to other organizations globally. Patient Care The ATS supports and fosters the highest quality of patient care. It evaluates the relationships between healthcare delivery, healthcare costs, and healthcare policy. The society establishes, reviews, and revises guidelines for optimal patient care. It promotes the development and application of ethical standards in patient care. Advocacy The ATS advocates for high-quality and cost-effective patient care. It advises, cooperates, and participates with government and non-government agencies on matters of mutual interest, including clinical practice and research. The society engages in activities aimed at preventing lung disease, promoting lung health, and enhancing patient care worldwide. Conferences The ATS holds its annual international conference in May. This event attracts approximately 15,000 physicians and scientists from around the world.
